Schema interchange fabric

A shared model
for your schemas.

UMF lets tools read and work with schemas from different systems without throwing away the details that make each one useful.

A database column, an API field and a domain model can describe the same data differently. UMF keeps those descriptions together, so your tools can use common metadata and still inspect the original.

Tools read the metadata they need. Support varies by format and operation.

What your tools can read

Fields, types, defaults, allowed values, keys and relationships give consumers a common starting point. Extensions hold the details specific to a database, schema language or domain.

Native details

An integer type alone doesn't tell you its range. A timestamp doesn't tell you its timezone rules. UMF keeps native refinements alongside shared metadata.

Unfamiliar metadata

A tool can carry an extension it doesn't understand. The content stays in the document, and validation tells you which parts it couldn't check.

Translation results

When a target can't express a source constraint, a projection reports the gap and retains the source. You can inspect what the generated schema will actually enforce.

Start with the library

Read and write JSON or YAML, inspect metadata, validate documents and work with native schema formats. The browser demo shows how unfamiliar content survives a read-and-write cycle.
